title: Dynamic zone arbitrator: combine percentile divergence and path-integrity scoring for region routing
creator: Liam O'Connor
description: Design and implement a zone arbitration component that uses percentile divergence (p50 versus p95) together with a path-integrity network score to pick the optimal region and tier for inference requests. The goal is to reduce user-visible tail latency regressions while preserving throughput and minimizing unnecessary variant fallbacks. This ticket covers design, prototype implementation, simulation against historical telemetry, and a staged rollout plan with observability and rollback paths.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A prototype service computes per-region scores combining latency percentiles and network health indicators. 2) Integration tests demonstrate the router switches to higher-integrity regions when p95 breaches configured thresholds while keeping p50 bias for cost-sensitive tiers. 3) Simulated traffic replay shows reduced tail-latency incidents by >= 30% for the tested workload without increasing average token cost by > 5%. 4) Dashboard panels for p50, p95, packet-loss, TCP RTT, circuit-eviction counts and fallback-rate are added. 5) Canary rollout plan documented with automatic rollback criteria.
comments: 2026-02-11: Kickoff meeting notes added to Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/zone-arbitrator-design. Decided on dual-signal scoring: percentile divergence ratio and path-integrity composite (pkt_loss, retransmits, tcp_rtt).

2026-02-18: Early prototype implemented in routing simulator. Basic scoring formula: score = w1 * normalized(p95/p50) + w2 * normalized(path_integrity). We normalize each signal to 0..1 and invert so higher means better. Default weights w1=0.6, w2=0.4 (tunable).

2026-02-24: Simulation against last 90 days of telemetry shows p95 spike reduction of 34% on test cohort (mobile-heavy). Average per-token cost increased 2.1% when forcing regional failover; acceptable within SLO. Saved simulation outputs to Drive: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/zone-arb-sims-2026

2026-03-01: Review feedback from Miguel Santos: prefer EWMA smoothing on path metrics with a 5-minute half-life to avoid flip-flopping, and keep a hysteresis window on percentile divergence to avoid oscillation during transient bursts. Added as follow-up task.
2026-03-04: Security review flagged telemetry aggregation scope for Private deployments. Added configuration toggle to disable telemetry-sharing and fall back to local-only scores for VPC customers.
2026-03-08: Integration PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/4567. Initial benchmarks in CI show negligible throughput overhead (<1%).

2026-03-12: Performance deep-dive with SRE: discovered that some POPs report stale RTT metrics; added staleness penalty to path-integrity calculation and a fallback to last-known-good when staleness < 2m.
notes_and_risks: Risks: - Over-reactive routing could increase egress/cost by shifting traffic to more expensive regions; mitigate by tier-aware weight adjustments. - Telemetry staleness can cause incorrect routing decisions; mitigate with staleness penalty and conservative hysteresis. - Private deployments may lack cross-pop telemetry; ensure config to use local-only scoring.
rollout_plan: 1) Unit + integration tests in staging. 2) Canary 1% of traffic for non-enterprise hosted customers for 48h with auto-rollback on p95 increase > 5% or error-rate increase > 0.5%. 3) Expand to 10% with monitoring for 72h. 4) Enable for dedicated pools with opt-in. 5) Add opt-out flag for Private deployments until customer telemetry opt-in is verified.
implementation_notes: - Implement scoring as a separate library so Dedicated/Private can reuse. - Provide config knobs: weights, hysteresis windows, EWMA half-life, staleness thresholds, cost-penalty cap. - When score difference between top-2 regions < delta_threshold, prefer affinity to preserve cache locality. - Fallback model variant selection: prefer quantized variant only after region-level failover persists > 30s and variant quality regressed within configured threshold.
